symptoms: Concentric dark brown target-board rings on older lower leaves
Chlorotic yellow halo surrounding brown necrotic lesions
Collar rot on stems and dark sunken leathery lesions at stem end of fruit
Progressive defoliation from ground level upward
immediate_actions: Prune heavily infected lower leaves showing target-board rings and burn or bury away from the field
Avoid overhead sprinkler irrigation to keep foliar canopy dry
Disinfect shears and pruning implements using 70% isopropyl alcohol between plants
cultural_control: Implement 3-year crop rotation with non-solanaceous crops (e.g., maize, pulses)
Mulch soil with clean straw or plastic to prevent rain splashback from soil onto lower foliage
Maintain adequate plant spacing (60 x 45 cm) for optimal canopy air circulation
biological_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum or Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 5 g/L water during early vegetative stage
Neem oil 1500 ppm @ 3 ml/L as a preventive antifungal barrier
tomato__early_blight.monitoring_guidance: Scout the field twice weekly starting from the 3rd week after transplanting, paying close attention to shaded lower leaves.
tomato__early_blight.publication: TNAU AgriTech Portal & ICAR-IIHR Vegetable Pathology Manual

symptoms: Water-soaked pale green to dark brown irregular foliar lesions
Delicate white fungal-like sporulation on underside of leaves in humid conditions
Rapid wilting and browning of foliage resembling frost burn
Firm, dark, greasy rot on green fruit
immediate_actions: Immediately rogue out and destroy severely blighted plants to stop rapid air-borne zoospore spread
Halt all overhead watering immediately; ensure furrow or drip irrigation only
Alert neighboring farms if high humidity (>90%) and cool nights (15-20°C) persist
cultural_control: Use certified disease-free transplants and resistant cultivars (e.g., Arka Rakshak, Kashi Adarsh)
Avoid planting adjacent to potato fields
Ensure elevated ridges and beds for rapid soil drainage
biological_control: Preventive sprays of Trichoderma viride @ 5 g/L during cool moist weather
Bacillus subtilis foliar formulation @ 10 g/L
tomato__late_blight.monitoring_guidance: Daily scouting is essential when temperatures stay between 15-22°C with persistent leaf wetness >10 hours.
tomato__late_blight.source: ICAR - Indian Institute of Vegetable Research (IIVR)
tomato__late_blight.publication: ICAR Integrated Pest Management in Solanaceous Crops

symptoms: Small, angular, dark brown to black water-soaked lesions on leaves
Lesion centers dry up and tear away leaving a ragged appearance
Black scab-like elevated spots on green fruit surrounded by a white halo
Extensive leaf drop leading to sunscald on exposed fruit
immediate_actions: Never enter or work in wet fields as bacteria spread instantaneously via water film
Remove severely spotted seedlings and avoid working with damp foliage
Sterilize all stakes, cages, and tools in a 10% bleach solution
cultural_control: Treat seeds with hot water (50°C for 25 minutes) before sowing
Purchase certified pathogen-free seeds from reputable seed agencies
Avoid handling seedlings during high relative humidity
biological_control: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed
Bacteriophage biological sprays if certified commercial formulations are available
tomato__bacterial_spot.monitoring_guidance: Examine underside of young leaves for water-soaked greasy specks following heavy rainfall and wind storms.
tomato__bacterial_spot.publication: TNAU Technical Bulletin on Bacterial Diseases of Vegetables

symptoms: Numerous small circular spots (2-3 mm) with gray or tan centers and dark brown margins
Tiny black pycnidia (fruiting bodies) clearly visible in center of mature spots with hand lens
Severe yellowing of affected leaves followed by complete leaf drop
Progresses rapidly upward from oldest bottom leaves
immediate_actions: Prune bottom 12 inches of foliage as soon as first clusters set to reduce splash inoculation
Collect and dispose fallen leaves away from field
Irrigate early in the morning so sun quickly dries foliar canopy
cultural_control: Deep plowing of field residues after harvest to bury overwintering pycnidia
Maintain strict weed control, especially solanaceous nightshade weeds
Stake and cage plants to keep foliage elevated off soil
biological_control: Bio-agent foliar application of Trichoderma harzianum @ 4 g/L water
Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) spray at 10-day intervals
tomato__septoria_leaf_spot.monitoring_guidance: Check lower leaves weekly after prolonged cloudy or rainy weather.
tomato__septoria_leaf_spot.publication: Management of Foliar Diseases in Solanaceous Crops

symptoms: Pale green to yellow diffuse spots on upper leaf surfaces
Olive-green to velvety brown mold growth directly underneath on leaf undersides
Infected leaves curl, wither, and drop prematurely
Primarily affects greenhouse and polyhouse tomato crops with high humidity
immediate_actions: Increase greenhouse ventilation and air movement using fans or open side curtains
Lower relative humidity below 85% inside the canopy
Remove severely covered lower leaves to improve airflow
cultural_control: Provide adequate plant spacing and prune suckers regularly
Adopt drip irrigation exclusively
Keep night temperatures warm enough to prevent condensation on foliage
biological_control: Foliar application of Ampelomyces quisqualis or Bacillus amyloliquefaciens @ 5 g/L
Potassium bicarbonate preventive foliar spray @ 3 g/L
tomato__leaf_mold.monitoring_guidance: Inspect undersides of mid-canopy leaves inside polyhouses or sheltered fields.
tomato__leaf_mold.publication: Protected Cultivation of Tomato: Disease Management

symptoms: Severe stunting and erect bushy appearance of plants
Marked upward cupping, curling, and reduction in leaf size
Pronounced interveinal chlorosis (yellowing) with green veins on new growth
Flower abortion and failure to set fruit
immediate_actions: Immediately uproot and destroy infected viral symptomatic plants in plastic bags
Install yellow sticky traps (15-20 per acre) immediately to monitor and capture whitefly vectors
Do NOT compost virus-infected plants
cultural_control: Grow virus-tolerant / resistant hybrids (e.g., Arka Ananya, US-440)
Raise nursery seedlings under 40-mesh insect-proof nylon net
Erect 2 rows of barrier crops like maize, sorghum, or pearl millet around the tomato field perimeter
biological_control: Foliar spray of Lecanicillium lecanii (Verticillium lecanii) @ 5 g/L to suppress whitefly nymphs
Azadirachtin 1% (10,000 ppm) @ 1.5 ml/L water
tomato__yellow_leaf_curl.monitoring_guidance: Monitor underside of young tender shoots in early morning for whitefly (Bemisia tabaci) populations.

symptoms: Uniform vibrant green foliage without spots, chlorosis, or curling
Firm, well-developed leaf veins and healthy petioles
Normal turgidity and balanced canopy expansion
immediate_actions: Maintain current balanced irrigation and fertigation schedule
Continue routine twice-weekly scouting of lower canopy
Ensure proper trellising and staking as plant loads increase
cultural_control: Balanced N-P-K nutrition with micronutrient supplement (calcium and boron to prevent blossom end rot)
Mulching to conserve root zone moisture
biological_control: Preventive application of Panchagavya (3%) or Jeevamrutha as bio-stimulant at 15-day intervals
tomato__healthy.monitoring_guidance: Regular visual scouting for early detection of pests like thrips, aphids, and fruit borers.
tomato__healthy.source: TNAU Package of Practices - Horticultural Crops
tomato__healthy.publication: Good Agricultural Practices (GAP) for Tomato Cultivation

symptoms: Dark brown to black angular spots with characteristic concentric rings on older leaves
Leaves turn yellow and dry up, remaining attached to the haulm
Tubers develop brown, sunken, corky dry rot beneath skin
immediate_actions: Avoid harvesting tubers during damp weather to prevent spore transfer into storage
Maintain adequate nitrogen and potassium fertility; stressed plants are significantly more susceptible
Destroy and bury infected haulms after dehaulming
cultural_control: Crop rotation with cereals, maize, or legumes for 2-3 years
Ensure certified disease-free seed tubers
Dehaulm (kill haulms) 10-15 days before harvest to thicken tuber skin
biological_control: Trichoderma viride seed tuber treatment @ 4 g/kg tuber
Neem seed kernel extract 5% foliar spray
potato__early_blight.monitoring_guidance: Scout bottom leaves starting 45 days after planting, particularly after intermittent rainfall followed by sunny days.
potato__early_blight.source: ICAR - Central Potato Research Institute (CPRI), Shimla
potato__early_blight.publication: CPRI Technical Bulletin: Potato Pathology in Subtropical Plains

symptoms: Water-soaked irregular patches on leaf margins and tips that turn dark brown to black rapidly
White cottony mildew growth visible on under-surface of lesions in morning humidity
Rapid blighting of the entire canopy with a characteristic decaying odor
Tubers show brown to purplish sunken surface rot and granular reddish-brown flesh
immediate_actions: Execute immediate protective fungicide spray upon first forecast warning of late blight conditions
If disease exceeds 20% canopy damage near maturity, cut haulms (dehaulming) to protect tubers from infection
Never wash infected tubers before cold storage
cultural_control: Plant resistant varieties like Kufri Girdhari, Kufri Himalini, Kufri Mohan
Adequate earthing up (20-25 cm ridge height) to prevent zoospores washing down to tubers
Use certified cold-store seed tubers from verified seed producers
biological_control: Trichoderma harzianum soil and foliar application as early preventive measure
potato__late_blight.monitoring_guidance: Utilize INDO-BLIGHTCAST weather-based forecaster: watch for temperatures 10-20°C with relative humidity >85% for 48 consecutive hours.
potato__late_blight.publication: Potato Late Blight Forecast and Containment Guidelines

symptoms: Robust lush green foliage, sturdy stems, and clean leaflets without discoloration
immediate_actions: Continue scheduled earthing-up to prevent tuber greening by sunlight
Maintain uniform soil moisture without water stagnation
cultural_control: Balanced NPK 120:100:120 kg/ha with timely top dressing of nitrogen
Regular de-weeding to avoid alternate host plants
biological_control: Bio-fertilizers Azotobacter and Phosphobacteria application @ 2.5 kg/ha
potato__healthy.monitoring_guidance: Check aphid counts (Myzus persicae) on leaf undersides to maintain seed plot quality.

symptoms: Small circular to irregular dark brown water-soaked spots with yellow chlorotic halos
Spots coalesce causing extensive blighting and premature leaf shedding
Raised wart-like rough brownish lesions on green chilli pods
immediate_actions: Refrain from spray operations or weeding while crop canopy is wet
Remove severely infested lower leaves and destroy away from field
Avoid excessive nitrogen fertilization which produces succulent susceptible leaf tissue
cultural_control: Seed treatment with hot water (50°C for 25 min) or Streptocycline 100 ppm for 30 min
Adopt raised bed cultivation with furrow irrigation
Crop rotation with maize or sorghum for 2 seasons
biological_control: Seed treatment with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 10 g/kg seed and soil application @ 2.5 kg/ha
Foliar spray of Bacillus subtilis @ 5 g/L
chilli__bacterial_spot.monitoring_guidance: Monitor fields closely following monsoon showers and high wind events.
chilli__bacterial_spot.publication: TNAU Crop Protection Guide for Spices & Condiments

symptoms: Vigorous green foliage with smooth shiny leaf surfaces, upright branching, and healthy blossoms
immediate_actions: Maintain consistent drip irrigation; avoid drought followed by heavy flooding which causes blossom drop
Monitor for thrips, mites, and aphids
cultural_control: Installation of blue sticky traps for thrips and yellow traps for aphids/whiteflies (12 traps/acre)
Balanced NPK fertilization with micronutrient foliar spray (Zinc, Boron)
biological_control: Neem seed kernel extract (NSKE 5%) preventive spray every 15 days
chilli__healthy.monitoring_guidance: Weekly scouting of growing tips and underside of young leaves.
chilli__healthy.source: TNAU Horticultural College and Research Institute

symptoms: Water-soaked stripes starting from leaf tips and margins, expanding into wavy yellowish-white lesions
Milky bacterial exudate oozing from cut edges of infected leaves when placed in water (ooze test positive)
Severe 'Kresek' seedling wilt phase causing complete seedling collapse
Straw-colored dried leaves looking bleached in the sun
immediate_actions: Drain the field immediately to reduce standing water humidity and eliminate bacterial swimming dispersal
Withhold all top-dressing of nitrogen fertilizer immediately; split application only after disease arrest
Avoid clip pruning of seedling tips during transplanting
cultural_control: Plant resistant rice varieties (e.g., Improved Samba Mahsuri, CO 51, CR Dhan 800)
Apply potassium fertilizer @ 50 kg/ha in two splits to enhance plant tissue resistance
Maintain clean bunds and eliminate wild rice and Cyperus weeds
biological_control: Seedling dip in Pseudomonas fluorescens (0.2%) suspension for 30 minutes before transplanting
Foliar spray of fresh cow dung extract (20%) which exhibits antagonistic bacterial activity
rice__bacterial_blight.monitoring_guidance: Check outer leaf tips across the field after cyclones, storms, or heavy rain accompanied by strong winds.
rice__bacterial_blight.source: ICAR - National Rice Research Institute (NRRI), Cuttack
rice__bacterial_blight.publication: NRRI Disease Bulletin: Bacterial Blight Management in Lowland Rice

symptoms: Isolated oval or circular dark brown sesame-seed shaped spots on leaves
Mature lesions feature gray or whitish centers surrounded by a dark brown margin with a yellow halo
Discoloration and blackening of glumes leading to unfilled chaffy grains
Particularly prevalent in nutrient-deficient, poorly drained, or sandy soils
immediate_actions: Apply potassium and zinc nutrition if deficiency is suspected; Brown Spot is an indicator of poor soil fertility
Maintain continuous shallow submergence of 2-3 cm; avoid drying out the field
Treat seeds before sowing in the next season
cultural_control: Soil application of recommended NPK along with FYM @ 12.5 t/ha or vermicompost
Soil correction for zinc deficiency using Zinc Sulphate @ 25 kg/ha
Use certified healthy seed paddy
biological_control: Seed treatment with Trichoderma viride @ 4 g/kg seed
Foliar spray of Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 2.5 kg/ha mixed in 500 L water
rice__brown_spot.monitoring_guidance: Scout leaves at tillering and panicle initiation stages, especially in drought-prone or rainfed uplands.

symptoms: Small, angular, slightly raised, leaden-black spots on leaf blades
Lesions remain distinct and do not coalesce
Under moist weather, the epidermis ruptures releasing black powdery mass of teliospores
Leaves turn yellow and die prematurely from the tip downwards
immediate_actions: Avoid excessive late nitrogen top-dressing
Keep field well-aerated and avoid excessive plant density
Burn or plow under stubble after harvest to destroy teliospore survival
cultural_control: Balanced fertilization based on Soil Health Card recommendations
Adopt SRI (System of Rice Intensification) spacing (25 x 25 cm) for airy canopy
biological_control: Foliar spray of Trichoderma harzianum @ 5 g/L
Neem cake soil application @ 150 kg/ha
rice__leaf_smut.monitoring_guidance: Scout flag leaves and upper leaves during grain filling stages.
rice__leaf_smut.publication: Fungal Diseases of Rice in India

symptoms: Tiny reddish-brown to rusty streaks running parallel to leaf veins
Streaks enlarge into dark brown to black elliptical spots with light gray sunken centers
Massive coalescing of spots leading to rapid drying and scorching of entire leaf blades
Premature ripening of bunches with unmarketable undersized fingers
immediate_actions: De-leafing: Cut off infected portions or entire severely dried leaves and place them face-down on the ground to reduce ascospore air discharge
Ensure proper drainage trenches in the plantation to remove standing monsoon water
Desucker plants regularly to maintain a maximum of 1 mother and 1 daughter sucker per stool
cultural_control: Plant resistant or tolerant banana cultivars (e.g., FHIA hybrids where adapted)
Maintain wide spacing (2.1 x 2.1 m) to reduce canopy humidity
Adequate potassium fertilization to strengthen leaf cuticle resistance
biological_control: Foliar spray of mineral oil (Banole or horticultural mineral oil) @ 10 ml/L as an ovicide/fungicide barrier
Trichoderma viride foliar spray @ 5 g/L
banana__black_sigatoka.monitoring_guidance: Weekly tracking of youngest leaf with streaks (YLS) on 10 marked plants across the grove.
banana__black_sigatoka.source: ICAR - National Research Centre for Banana (NRCB), Tiruchirappalli
banana__black_sigatoka.publication: NRCB Technical Bulletin No. 34: Integrated Sigatoka Disease Management

symptoms: Progressive yellowing and wilting of leaves starting from inner younger whorls
Premature yellowing and uneven ripening of fruit fingers with internal dark reddish-brown dry pulp rot
Vascular discoloration: Yellow, orange to dark brown strands visible when pseudostem is cut
Floral bracts wilt, blacken, and drop prematurely
immediate_actions: Debudding: Remove male flower bud (bell) using a forked wooden stick immediately after last hand has formed to prevent insect vector transmission
Disinfect all machetes and cutting tools with 20% sodium hypochlorite (bleach) or flame after every plant
Sterilize the surrounding soil of affected mats with bleaching powder @ 25 g/mat
cultural_control: Single Diseased Plant Removal (SDPR): Cut infected plant at ground level and destroy, rather than uprooting entire mat
Use certified pathogen-free tissue-cultured plantlets
Never use suckers from unknown or wilt-affected plantations
biological_control: Soil drenching with Pseudomonas fluorescens @ 20 g/mat at planting and at 3rd month
banana__bacterial_wilt.monitoring_guidance: Scout flowering plants bi-weekly for male bell wilting and premature fruit finger yellowing.
banana__bacterial_wilt.source: ICAR-NRCB Tiruchirappalli & FAO Banana Pathology Guidelines
banana__bacterial_wilt.publication: NRCB Guidelines for Bacterial Wilt Containment in Cavendish & Nendran

symptoms: Expansive, broad, vibrant green leaves with sturdy midribs and clean pseudostems free from discoloration
immediate_actions: Maintain consistent drip irrigation (20-25 L/plant/day depending on stage)
Provide bamboo or wooden propping to supporting bunches as bunch weight increases
cultural_control: Balanced nutrient schedule: 200g N, 60g P, 300g K per plant applied in split doses
Regular desuckering to direct plant energy into primary bunch filling
biological_control: Apply Arbuscular Mycorrhizal Fungi (AMF) @ 50 g/plant and Azospirillum @ 25 g/plant at planting
banana__healthy.monitoring_guidance: Regular inspection for pseudostem weevil boreholes and aphid colonies near throat.
